answer: Multimodal LLM agents (also called large multimodal agents) are AI systems in which a large language model acts as the reasoning "brain" of an agent that can perceive inputs beyond text — such as images, video, audio, or GUI screens — and then plan and take actions in an environment to accomplish a goal. They are typically described in terms of four core components: perception (encoding multimodal inputs), planning (decomposing the task and reasoning about steps), action (calling tools, APIs, or controlling software/robots), and memory (storing context and past experience). Compared with text-only LLM agents, this extension lets the system handle richer, more nuanced user queries — for example reading a chart, navigating a web page, or guiding a robot — which also raises harder evaluation and reliability challenges.
